subject.title: [memory-core] SQLite unbounded growth: memory_index_chunks + memory_embedding_cache tables have no retention policy, will fill disk over time

question: Should memory-core enforce a bounded embedding-cache default and automatic rebuild-safe index retention, and if so what persistence and eviction contract should existing agent databases receive?
rationale: The repository already exposes a cache-size setting, but selecting a default, eviction semantics, and a possible on-disk representation migration changes user storage and search behavior rather than repairing a clearly isolated defect.

options.title: Define bounded derived-cache defaults
options.body: Set and document a conservative plugin-owned default cap, retain an explicit override, and prove pruning plus re-index recovery on upgrade.

options.title: Keep opt-in limits
options.body: Preserve the current optional cap and improve diagnostics/docs so operators can size cache retention themselves.

options.title: Split representation migration
options.body: Address retention first and consider JSON-to-BLOB conversion only after a dedicated migration and compatibility design.

recommendation.title: Define bounded derived-cache defaults
recommendation.body: Set and document a conservative plugin-owned default cap, retain an explicit override, and prove pruning plus re-index recovery on upgrade.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent public memory-core contribution history is the strongest available routing signal, though direct blame/history verification was blocked.
